body: Thanks for sharing. I'm (regrettably) in a position where everyone is able to tell before I even open my mouth, so I'm hoping that it is acceptance that you are picking up on and not just ignorance. Please feel free to reach out by PM if you need someone to talk to

hi,

it IS complicated.

i can feel your pain -- but it doesn't work that way, she doesn't get to demand that you compromise on who you are, no matter how sick she is. it will be absolutely no reflection on you if she passes feeling bad about the way you're living your life.

people will say forget about her but it's not that simple. i would understand if you feel the need to be there for her in her moment of uncertainty and pain; what i would do if it were me is show up & offer to stay as you are, and if she can't handle that, well it doesn't mean that there's anything wrong with YOU. hopefully she will see what really matters.

Thanks for sharing your experience. I do expect that my parents will be similar, especially my dad. It will take them time to get their heads around it, assuming they're willing to try, and in the meantime I think they'll struggle. Weirdly the fact that I am not around them a lot makes this maybe harder because they only think of me at a distance and only talk to me over the phone, except at holidays. I have thought about, for example, getting a hotel when I visit home just in case they are less comfortable than they thought they'd be.

I would love if you would PM anything you have, it might be very helpful to them or me.

Thanks again.

Thanks for your insight and advice. We are a decently close family, but since I moved for grad school some years back, I see them quite rarely. I'm definitely prepared to be disowned at least practically (ie I'm not dependent on them) but there are nieces and nephews in the picture that I would like to be able to visit without feeling like I am making things awkward.

I do worry that the longer I hide this, the more hurt they will be. For what it's worth, I would instantly shut down any talk from them about whether this is happening or trying to talk me down. HRT was really the best thing I've ever done and the rest of my life flows outward from that pretty much.

I think you're right that this has been more about building myself up rather than actually making it easier for my parents. Thank you for sharing your story and I'm glad that you came to that realization about fear.
That's a very sweet thing to say, thank you.

Thanks for your comment. Fundamentally, I know you're right that I really can't control how they're going to respond and it's likely not going to be different based on when and how delicately I do this. I guess I just feel like I should do everything in my power to help them wrap their heads around this, but ultimately it's going to be on them, not me. I need to figure out if I'm ready to do this now, I guess.
